newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM precious metals end mixed, palladium higher.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM precious metals end mixed, palladium higher.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo precious metals futures ended mixed on Thursday, with gold little changed after a day of range-trading, while palladium settled slightly higher after shedding most of its early gains, traders said.
Gold futures ranged from four yen per gram lower to two yen higher. Benchmark June was off one yen at 1,212 yen.
"Interest in gold futures was thin as market players were tending to be sidelined to watch if spot gold tests the downside support at $330.00 per ounce," one trader said.
Spot gold was quoted at $332.20/70 per ounce at 0721 GMT, against $331.10/60 in New York on Wednesday.
In the bullion market, gold was supported by moderate short-covering while hedge-selling by Australian producers, which helped gold to a fresh four-year lows on Wednesday, faded on Thursday.

Gold bullion prices in the local Tokyo market slid further to around 30 U.S. cents per ounce above the world benchmark, down from about 60 U.S. cents late last week. The fall reflected weak Japan gold demand, the traders said.
Palladium shed early gains on long-liquidation to end higher after animated short-covering boosted some months to daily limit highs intraday, they said.

Although the Russian platinum group metals agency said Russian PGM contracted sales to Japan would resume on July 10, sentiment toward PGM remained bullish as Russia was no longer a stable supplier. "As the physical PGM market, especially palladium, was extremely tight after the six-month sales suspension. Accumulated short positions in palladium by private investors may cause further volatility," one PGM trader said.
Benchmark June palladium ended up six yen at 531 yen.
Benchmark June was off seven yen at 1,350 yen.
Benchmark June silver was up 0.3 yen per 10 grams at 173.9
